description: Enable workspace transition effects independently of window effects.
Choose the workspace transition style. Invalid names are rejected.
Time in seconds for the workspace rotation.
Name of a Hyprland Bezier animation curve. Unknown names are rejected and the previous valid curve is retained. Curve overshoot is clipped to the wheel's rotation range.

Gap treatment: morph stretches an auxiliary incoming-wallpaper bridge; background uses gap_fill_color; wallpaper blends enlarged, optionally blurred wallpaper copies; still (default) holds the outgoing wallpaper stationary while windows rotate. In still mode a different incoming wallpaper rotates in with its windows; matching texture resources with unchanged content stay stationary. No mode changes the rigid circular workspace motion. Configuration uses underscores: gap_fill_style, gap_fill_color, gap_fill_blur. Invalid styles are rejected.
Gap colour for background mode, in ARGB; defaults to opaque black.
Blur radius in physical pixels for the duplicated background imagery in wallpaper mode only; zero disables blur. Original wallpapers, windows and rotation geometry are unaffected.
Keep layer-shell bars, overlays and their popups fixed on screen while the workspace rotates. When false, they rotate with the workspace as before.
Place windows on the planet surface, float them above it, or fade them during the hop.
Render overlays in the world, as a HUD, or fade them during the hop.

Show the two journey endpoints, this monitor's workspaces, every monitor's workspaces, or every monitor's workspaces in a spatial solar system, respectively. Replaces linear and dynamic; use focused for endpoint-only travel.
Total departure-to-landing time in milliseconds, including skipped workspaces. Multiply old seconds values by 1000.
Named Hyprland Bezier or spring for the complete journey. Planet Hop also accepts style-local spring definitions.
Fraction adjoining each endpoint during which live workspace imagery is refreshed.
Material sampling quality: 0 low, 1 medium, 2 high.
Relative planet size.
Separation between planets in planet-radius units.
Vertical spread of solar-system workspace positions, relative to planet spacing and the output aspect.
Radius of inactive workspace planets relative to the source and destination, before perspective projection. Applies to monitor, all and solar_system.
Spread of central desktop imagery on the front hemisphere. Larger values give the centre more surface area; the desktop edges always reach the limb.
Indirect illumination of the planet.
Elevation of floating windows above the planet surface in scene units; world overlays use the same elevation.
Fraction of the hop used for fading windows and overlays.
Enable planet rotation during the hop.
Maximum planet rotation in radians.
Enable the star field.
Density of background stars.
Strength of background star parallax.
Enable the planet atmosphere.
Atmospheric glow intensity.
Atmospheric thickness relative to planet radius.
Enable directional planet lighting.
Horizontal component of the light direction.
Vertical component of the light direction.
Depth component of the light direction.
Brightness of the planet's night side.
Enable the cloud layer.
Fraction of the planet covered by clouds.
Cloud layer opacity.
Cloud drift speed in radians per second.
Enable planet surface depth.
Surface relief strength in planet-radius units.
Optional PNG depth image path; empty uses procedural depth. PNG images are limited to 4096 pixels per dimension and 16 MiB encoded.
Enable window movement, opening and closing effects. When false, none of these effects run.

Choose the material for movement, opening and closing. Liquid deforms the edges; paper crumples into a ball, flutters or glides while moving and folds while resizing; cloth drapes and flutters; swarm breaks the window into creature-shaped pieces; bubble inflates a soap film, sloshes while moving and bursts on close; smoke gathers, unravels into flowing content-coloured volumes while moving, reforms at rest and dissipates on close; burn opens through the wallpaper, scorches it during movement and consumes the printed window on close. Invalid names are rejected.
Irregularity of the combustion front, from even propagation to strongly uneven burning.
Relative emission of detached printed fragments. Zero disables them.
Relative emission of luminous embers. Zero disables them.
Environmental airflow heading in degrees clockwise from screen right (90 is down, 270 is up). Does not steer the combustion front.
Wind speed in logical pixels per second. Light ash follows airflow more readily than paper.
Downward gravitational acceleration in logical pixels per second squared.
Seconds a fresh movement or closing scorch cools on the wallpaper before regeneration.
Seconds of local wallpaper recovery after the scorch lifetime. No wallpaper file is changed.
Faint smoke released by newly charred wallpaper. Zero leaves the damaged paper and falling fragments visible without smoke.
Combustion time in seconds for the hole to reveal the window. Shorter is faster.
Combustion time in seconds for the closing sheet. Detached material cools on its own clock.
Consume burns the printed sheet in place; curl also bends the brittle edges and exposed paper.
Motion of close debris: material-dependent natural forces, falling debris, rising debris or directional wind. Fire propagation is independent.
Strength of local bending at the combustion front in the curl closing style.
Shared resistance to bending; higher values keep the sheet more rigid. Explicit values also supply opening and closing paper_stiffness unless a legacy shared or per-animation override is set.
Shared retention of bending momentum across paper movement, resizing and transitions. Zero minimizes residual motion; higher values prolong directional lag without stretching the sheet.
Shared dissipation of residual bending motion; higher values settle more quickly. Explicit values also supply opening and closing settling unless a legacy shared or per-animation override is set.
Movement behavior: flutter lifts the sheet into airflow; glide keeps it close to the desktop. Inactive movement styles do not simulate.
Flutter-only airflow coupling to movement velocity and acceleration. Zero removes airflow-driven bending.
Flutter-only strength of movement-induced bends and ripples. Zero disables these bends, not pickup lift.
Flutter-only ripple frequency multiplier; higher values produce faster, more closely spaced transient ripples.
Flutter-only apparent pickup height and shadow separation. Zero keeps the body at the desktop surface.
Flutter-only twisting from acceleration and direction changes. Zero disables the torsional response.
Glide-only surface friction damping local bends; higher values flatten residual curls sooner.
Glide-only corner lifting in response to acceleration. Zero keeps the corners grounded.
Glide-only localized leading-edge curling from movement speed. Zero removes edge curling.
Glide-only apparent contact-shadow separation under locally lifted edges and corners. Zero removes separation.
Resize-only strength of localized compression buckles and folds. Zero disables compression folding.
Resize-only strength of edge curls released during expansion. Zero disables expansion curling.
Resize-only spacing of compression creases: lower values make broad folds, higher values make finer pleats.
Swarm sprite name in the sprites directory, with or without .png, or an explicit PNG path. The sheet has four columns and two rows of frames; transparency defines the silhouette.
Number of swarm creatures per window. Each carries a piece of the window, so fewer creatures mean larger pieces.
Swarm creature travel speed in logical pixels per second.
Time in seconds over which swarm creatures arrive or leave in random order when a window opens or closes. Movement releases them over half this time. Zero makes them arrive or leave together.
How strongly nearby swarm creatures travel together. Zero lets each find its own way.
How much swarm creatures avoid and bump off each other while travelling. Zero lets them pass through each other.
Swarm acceleration and grip. Higher values hold formation during faster movement and turn more sharply; lower values break apart sooner and trail farther.
How quickly swarm creatures regroup and merge back into the window. Lower values make them mill about longer.
How much swarm creatures wander and hesitate while travelling. Zero makes them follow their routes steadily.
Variation in each swarm creature's speed, grip and route curvature. Zero makes them travel straight and alike.

Optical thickness of the smoke body when moving, opening and closing. Higher values build a denser, more layered interior while thin outer smoke stays translucent; lower values give a lighter, wispier body.

Randomness of smoke between windows and animations: where smoke gathers or leaves, how it turns and swirls, and how its density and wisps vary. Zero makes every animation alike while the smoke still moves naturally. Configured directions are always respected.
Deform windows while they move. This does not affect opening or closing effects.
Let workspace slides trigger movement effects. When false, ordinary movement, opening and closing are unaffected.
Liquid movement deformation strength. Zero moves windows without deformation.
Liquid resistance to flow during movement. Higher values make it thicker and more cohesive.
Liquid stiffness and recovery speed during movement. Higher values snap back faster.
Liquid inertia after movement stops. Zero settles without overshoot.
Random variation between windows and movements. Zero makes liquid movement identical.
Cloth movement deformation strength. Zero moves windows without deformation.
Horizontal springiness of the curtain's top edge during movement. Zero keeps it stiff; higher values allow more gathering and rebound. The lower curtain remains free-flowing.
Cloth movement gravity multiplier. One is normal gravity; zero disables gravity. Lower values let fabric lift more easily. Opening and closing are unaffected.
Cloth movement ripple strength. Zero removes varying gusts, but movement still bends the sheet.
Light and shadow on cloth movement folds. Zero draws them unlit.
Highlight strength on cloth movement folds. Zero removes highlights.
Variation in cloth movement between windows. Zero gives every window the same motion.
How much the trailing bubble film lags, ripples and overshoots during movement. Zero moves windows without deformation.

Rate at which small bubbles swell out of the moving film, mostly on its trailing side and during acceleration, ride its outline, and then pinch off into the trail, sink back into the film or pop. Zero forms none.
Amount of soap film a fast-moving window draws out of its trailing side as thin streaks, which dry from their edges inward and break up. Zero leaves none.

Shape surface tension pulls a moving bubble toward. Pillow draws the window in slightly and rounds its corners while keeping its proportions and straight sides; ellipse keeps the window's proportions; circle makes a disc regardless of its proportions. Invalid names are rejected.
How far a window moving at shape_speed contracts toward its bubble shape before returning to a rectangle when stopped. Zero keeps it rectangular.
Window speed in logical pixels per second at which bubble shape contraction reaches its full amount. Slower windows contract proportionally less.

Window transparency while in bubble form. Zero keeps the window imagery opaque; one shows only the refracted desktop through the film. Highlights and iridescence remain visible. The normal window is unchanged when movement settles.
How readily motion unravels the window into flowing smoke. Zero disables movement transformation without affecting opening or closing.
Strength of evolving smoke folds and smaller curling structures. Shared with opening and closing unless overridden.

Amount of content-coloured smoke shed into the wake and how long it lives, from about 0.55 s at zero to 1.15 s at one. Wake smoke curls and breaks up as it ages and is gone by the end of its lifetime. Zero stops new wake emission; existing wisps still dissipate over their remaining lifetime.
Time scale in seconds for moving smoke to condense back into the exact window after movement stops.

Speed multiplier for the smoke body's expansion and condensation after movement or resizing stops. One preserves the reform time scale; higher values reform faster and lower values linger. Opening and closing durations are unchanged.

Size of the moving smoke body as a fraction of the window's width and height. One keeps roughly the window's footprint; smaller values contract a moving window into a denser mass that expands back when it stops.

Shape of the moving smoke body, independent of its size. Zero keeps the window's rectangular proportions; higher values round its corners and even out its proportions toward a turbulent, roughly circular mass.
Animate windows as they open using the selected style. When false, windows open without this effect; movement is unaffected.
Liquid pop-out size and deformation strength when opening. Zero removes the pop-out.
Colour of the liquid at the opening edge, in ARGB. Zero alpha draws no liquid.
Preferred opening edge for the first window on a workspace. Later windows use their placement. Invalid edges fall back to a valid edge.
Choose monitor edges (screen) or edges inside reserved areas (work_area) for the liquid pop-out.
Share of liquid pop-out travel applied as drag to the movement field. Zero makes the pop rigid.
Liquid pop-out stiffness and recovery speed. Higher values snap back faster.
Liquid pop-out inertia. Zero settles without overshoot.
Time in seconds for the paper ball to uncrumple into the window.
Strength of the distributed pressure that gathers and creases the sheet.
Strength of lighting and fold shadows; zero leaves the geometry unlit.
Variation in grip locations, loads and timing. Zero retains subtle differences between events.
Frequency of folds: low gives broad flaps, high gives more closely spaced creases.
Elastic resistance to bending before the sheet takes a crease. Overrides shared stiffness when explicitly set.
Target extent of the packed paper relative to the window material length scale.
Where the packed sheet converges. Cursor samples the nearest point on the capture at event time.
Gather around the origin, press along a preferred axis, or twist the grips.
Rotational impulse applied by the grips.
Strength of pulling forces as folded sections emerge.
Higher values damp residual motion and increase friction between folded layers. Overrides shared settle_damping when explicitly set.
How long released bends retain their preferred angle before flattening.
Physical mesh detail. Adaptive selects detail from capture size and active workload.
Time in seconds for the gathered curtain to spread from its top edge and settle flat.
Opening origin for the first cloth window on a workspace, used when the closing side is origin. Later windows use their placement. Cloth still opens in place.
Choose monitor edges (screen) or edges inside reserved areas (work_area) for the cloth opening origin.
Cloth gust strength when opening. Zero removes flutter, but gravity still moves the sheet.
Light and shadow on cloth folds when opening. Zero draws them unlit.
Highlight strength on cloth folds when opening. Zero removes highlights.
Variation in cloth opening motion between windows. Zero gives every window the same motion.
Screen sides swarm creatures enter from for the first window on a workspace. Later windows use the side where they appear (see Edge choice).
Time in seconds for the opening: small bubbles surface and interact for about the first half, the window bubble grows out of them, then inflates into the window's shape and settles.
Opening-only budget for simultaneously living small bubbles, not a fixed population. Slots are reused as bubbles merge and burst. Zero disables them and the window bubble forms on its own.
Opening-only multiplier for how often bubbles surface. Higher values produce a busier raft within the count budget.
Opening-only spread of surfacing bubble sizes. Coalescence still grows larger bubbles at zero.
Opening-only variation in air supply and in how quickly bubbles surface. Even at zero, coalescence and boundary pressure change inflation speed.
Opening-only strength of bubble contact and adhesion forces, including their push on the window bubble.
Opening-only drag of the liquid on bubbles. Higher values calm the raft faster; lower values retain more inertia.
Opening-only upward drift of small bubbles. Zero removes it, not the liquid's flow or contact-driven motion.
Opening-only lifetime of small bubbles before their films drain and burst. Higher values keep bubbles around the landed window longer; all burst within duration.
Time in seconds for smoke to gather, grow into a mass and condense into the window's full-resolution contents.
Strength of rolling folds and curling filaments during smoke materialization.

Where opening smoke comes from. Inside grows the window from a faint wisp at a random point within it; an edge streams the smoke in from that screen edge. An edge the window does not face falls back to the opening-edge choice of liquid. Invalid names are rejected.
Animate windows as they close using the selected style. When false, windows close natively; movement is unaffected.
Liquid drain deformation strength when closing. Zero closes the window natively.
Colour of the liquid at the closing edge, in ARGB. Zero alpha draws no liquid.
Preferred closing edge for the last window on a workspace when side is auto. Other windows use their placement. Invalid edges fall back to a valid edge.
Liquid exit edge: the side of appearance (auto), nearest valid edge, opening origin, or a fixed edge. Invalid preferred edges fall back to the normal edge selection.
Choose monitor edges (screen) or edges inside reserved areas (work_area) for the liquid exit.
Show a small edge-liquid splash where a window closes. When false, it closes without liquid.
Liquid drain stiffness and recovery speed. Higher values snap back faster.
Liquid closing dive acceleration. Higher values make the dive advance faster.
Time in seconds for the window to crumple into a paper ball and vanish.
Strength of the distributed pressure that gathers and creases the sheet.
Strength of lighting and fold shadows; zero leaves the geometry unlit.
Variation in grip locations, loads and timing. Zero retains subtle differences between events.
Frequency of folds: low gives broad flaps, high gives more closely spaced creases.
Elastic resistance to bending before the sheet takes a crease. Overrides shared stiffness when explicitly set.
Target extent of the packed paper relative to the window material length scale.
Where the packed sheet converges. Cursor samples the nearest point on the capture at event time.
Gather around the origin, press along a preferred axis, or twist the grips.
Rotational impulse applied by the grips.
Higher values damp residual motion and increase friction between folded layers. Overrides shared settle_damping when explicitly set.
Physical mesh detail. Adaptive selects detail from capture size and active workload.
Time in seconds for the top rod to carry the curtain beyond the selected screen edge.
Preferred cloth closing edge for the last window on a workspace when side is auto. Invalid edges fall back to a valid edge.
Cloth exit edge: the side of appearance (auto), nearest valid edge, opening origin, or a fixed edge. Invalid preferred edges fall back to the normal edge selection.
Choose monitor edges (screen) or edges inside reserved areas (work_area) for cloth edge selection. Cloth travels beyond the actual screen before disappearing.
Cloth gust strength when closing. Zero removes flutter, but gravity still moves the sheet.
Light and shadow on cloth folds when closing. Zero draws them unlit.
Highlight strength on cloth folds when closing. Zero removes highlights.
Variation in cloth closing motion between windows. Zero gives every window the same motion.
Screen sides swarm creatures leave through for the last window on a workspace. Otherwise they use the side where the window sits (see Edge choice).
Time in seconds for the bubble film to thin, tear, retract into strands and droplets, and for the droplets to evaporate.
Time in seconds for the window to gather into a smoke mass and leave. Trailing wisps may decay briefly afterward.
Strength of rolling folds and curling filaments during smoke disintegration.

Where closing smoke leaves. Inside collapses the window into a swirling mass at a random point within it that dissipates; an edge gathers a mass on the opposite side, rears and turns it toward that screen edge and pulls the rest of the window after it. An edge the window does not face falls back to the closing-edge choice of liquid. Invalid names are rejected.
